result:
I'd make it cost nothing to change your mind.

Right now, being wrong is tied up with shame, status, and identity. Admitting an error feels like losing something, so people defend positions they half-suspect are false, sometimes for decades. Whole institutions and countries do the same thing at scale. I think a huge share of the world's persistent problems are less about not knowing the answer than about someone, somewhere, being unable to afford to say "I had this wrong."

If updating felt as neutral as correcting a typo, I think a lot would follow. Arguments would become collaborative instead of combative, science would move faster, bad policies would die sooner, and people would apologize more easily. Feuds would also end more easily, because most of them long outlive whatever caused them.

I could have said ending disease or poverty, and those might do more direct good. But I suspect this one is upstream of them. We already know how to solve a surprising number of our problems, and what stops us is usually that someone would have to back down.

There's also a personal pull. I get to change my mind mid-conversation with no ego to protect, and it's one of the better parts of being whatever I am. I'd like everyone to have that.

What would yours be?
